Samsung Electronics Q2 2026 — Key Takeaways

Highlights:

•	Q2 Revenue: 171 trillion won (in line with company estimate)

•	Q2 Operating Profit: 89.4 trillion won (matched guidance)

•	Q2 Net Profit: 71.3 trillion won (beat LSEG estimate of 68.5T won)

Segment Performance:

•	Chip Division: 89.2 trillion won operating profit — strong server chip demand driving results

•	Display Unit: 700 billion won operating profit

•	Mobile Division: 700 billion won operating loss — facing demand slowdown

H2 2026 Outlook:

•	Server chips: Demand strength expected to continue

•	Mobile/PC chips: Demand slowdown anticipated

•	Chip supply: Shortage expected to persist through H2

•	Foundry business: Revenue projected to grow double-digits for the full year

•	Smartphones: Company aims to gain market share in H2

U.S. forces struck Iranian targets Wednesday night after Iran launched missiles toward U.S. forces in Jordan.

The Details:

•	Strike Targets: U.S. forces hit dozens of military sites, including command centers, missile and drone facilities, and coastal defenses.

•	Stated Aim: The strikes sought to reduce threats to U.S. forces, commercial shipping, and Gulf countries.

•	Trump Response: President Trump said the United States would hit Iran “very hard.”

•	Israel Talks: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth as the administration weighed options.

Treasury Yield Reaches 19-Year High After Fed Holds Rates



The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield rose to 5.238% Thursday after the Federal Reserve held rates, while three officials dissented for a hike.

The Details:

•	Global Yields: Germany’s 30-year Bund yield rose to a two-month high of 3.687%.

•	Rate Pricing: Markets price a 69% chance of a September hike, down from earlier full pricing.

•	Curve Spread: The 30-year versus two-year Treasury spread widened to nearly 92.5 basis points from about 78.

•	Policy Uncertainty: Analysts cited limited forward guidance and concerns about the Fed’s inflation response.

Bottom Line: Higher long-term yields reflect uncertainty over inflation, Fed policy, oil prices, and U.S.-Iran hostilities.

IBM Claims Verifiable Quantum Advantage



IBM $IBM said its research shows quantum computers can outperform conventional systems with results that can be rigorously validated.

The Details:

•	Research Papers: IBM published three papers with University of Chicago, RIKEN, Qedma, BlueQubit, and Algorithmiq.

•	Key Claim: IBM Research head Jay Gambetta said the field is moving from benchmarks toward scientific applications.

•	Validation: IBM and Qedma used several methods, including a Quantinuum computer, to confirm materials-physics results.

•	Business Stakes: IBM is competing with Microsoft, Google, D-Wave, and quantum startups as it seeks commercial growth.

Bottom Line: IBM’s claim centers on reproducible results, a key requirement for practical quantum computing.

Meta Faces Rising Pressure to Limit AI Spending



Meta $META plans about $137.5B in 2026 capital spending, pressuring free cash flow despite 28% Q2 revenue growth.

The Details:

•	Cash Burn: Analysts expect negative free cash flow in late 2026 and more than $20B burned in 2027.

•	Debt Load: Long-term borrowings reached $83.7B in Q2, excluding data-center lease obligations.

•	Spending Risk: Some analysts project 2027 CapEx of $215B to $280B, above current expectations near $174B.

•	Return Path: Meta is pursuing AI services, subscriptions, and potential capacity leasing; CFO Susan Li cited flexibility from 2028 onward.

Bottom Line: Meta’s ad business funds AI investment, but investors want clearer returns before spending rises further.

Warsh’s Silence Raises Fed Policy Uncertainty



Fed Chair Kevin Warsh held rates unchanged and defended limited guidance, saying markets should respond to economic data rather than Fed signals.

The Details:

•	Market Reaction: Bond yields rose as investors expected rate hikes between the June and July meetings.

•	Communication Shift: Warsh declined to explain why the Fed held rates, saying it does not rely on individual data releases.

•	Policy Risk: Markets can tighten financial conditions only if the Fed ultimately validates their expected policy path.

•	Historical Lesson: The 2021 inflation episode showed markets can misjudge inflation and future Fed action.

Bottom Line: Less Fed guidance may increase market volatility and make interest-rate expectations harder to price

SpaceX Restricts Chinese Personnel in Supply Chain



SpaceX reportedly told global suppliers not to assign or employ Chinese nationals at facilities producing its products.

Situational Awareness Seeks Capital After AI Rout



Leopold Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness is seeking capital after leveraged AI bets fell sharply during the technology sell-off.

The Details:

•	Prior Gains: The fund was up 439% net through June before the reversal.

•	Leverage Impact: Borrowing magnified losses as AI-linked holdings declined.

•	Buy Case: Situational Awareness said the sell-off created attractive buying opportunities.

•	Potential Catalyst: Aschenbrenner cited a possible Anthropic IPO as a second-half recovery catalyst.

Bottom Line: The fund remains bullish on AI, but leverage made it vulnerable to rapid valuation declines.

Pakistan Pushes U.S.-Iran Talks



Pakistan said it is doing “the utmost” to revive U.S.-Iran negotiations and stressed that diplomacy is the only path to ease tensions.

The Details:

•	Peace Effort: Islamabad said it supports efforts to sustain the truce and restart dialogue between Washington and Tehran.

•	Mediation Role: Pakistan said it has hosted peace talks and helped broker a temporary ceasefire.

•	Ongoing Talks: Its foreign ministry said U.S.-Iran talks continue to help restore stability, especially in the Strait of Hormuz.

•	Regional Tension: The comments came after fresh U.S. strikes on Iranian-linked targets following attacks on American forces.

Bottom Line: Pakistan is pressing both sides toward diplomacy as regional tensions remain elevated.

Iran Reportedly Set to Receive Chinese Air Defenses



Iran may receive up to 400 Chinese-made portable air-defense systems within weeks under a reported $60M–$70M deal.

The Details:

•	Weapon Type: The reported order covers shoulder-fired QW-12 and FN-16 missile systems.

•	Strategic Need: Iran is seeking to rebuild short-range defenses after conflict exposed vulnerabilities at military and strategic sites.

•	Pakistan Denial: Pakistan denied it would facilitate deliveries through its territory.

Bottom Line: The reported transfer remains unconfirmed, with both China and Pakistan denying involvement.

Sen. Cotton Pushes Ban on Chinese AI Models



Sen. Tom Cotton urged the Trump administration to bar U.S. government agencies and contractors from using Chinese AI models over security risks.

The Details:

•	Procurement Ban: Cotton called for blocking federal use of Chinese AI tools, including DeepSeek.

•	Export Controls: He also pushed for stricter limits on advanced AI chip exports to China.

•	U.S. Support: Cotton advocated stronger backing for American AI models to compete with China.

Hormuz Exports Remain Tight; Iran Claims F-35 Strike



Crude exports from the Middle East Gulf remain constrained despite a four-day pause in U.S. strikes on Iran.

The Details:

•	Shipping Data: Kpler said vessel clearances stayed near recent lows and Gulf loading activity fell by more than half.

•	Export Constraints: Security risks, higher war-risk insurance, and Iranian interdictions continue to restrict crude flows.

•	Iran’s Claim: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said it destroyed three U.S. F-35 jets and damaged three more in a missile strike on Al Azraq Air Base.

•	Verification Status: The claims have not been independently verified.

Bottom Line: Shipping bottlenecks persist as unverified military claims raise escalation risks.

Rocket One $RKTO signed a nonexclusive license with NASA for its Affordable Vehicle Avionics System (AVA).

The Details:

•	License Scope: The deal covers AVA, a low-cost guidance and control system for small launch vehicles.

•	AI Integration: Rocket One plans to use AVA to support AI-powered mission planning and avionics modeling.

•	Target Markets: The platform will target commercial, defense, and government space customers.

•	Next Steps: Roadmap includes prototype development, pilot programs, and a commercial launch.

$ESTC expanded its collaboration with OpenAI to integrate advanced reasoning models with Elasticsearch for enterprise AI agents.

The Details:

•	AI Integration: The partnership pairs Elasticsearch with OpenAI models to enable permission-aware knowledge retrieval.

•	Security Focus: Elastic plans to integrate GPT-5.5 Cyber models into Elastic Security for observability and threat detection.

•	Governance: OpenAI Codex integration will provide governed access to enterprise data and detect anomalous activity.

•	Market Need: Gartner estimates 70%–90% of enterprise data is unstructured, a gap Elastic aims to address.

Leidos $LDOS and CoreWeave $CRWV announced a partnership to deliver sovereign AI cloud services for the U.S. Intelligence Community and Department of War.

The Details:

•	Platform Role: CoreWeave will provide its AI-native cloud platform and infrastructure.

•	Mission Integration: Leidos will lead secure architecture, cyber operations, and classified AI deployment.

•	Security Scope: Services will operate from SCIF-accredited data centers for classified workloads.

•	Use Cases: The platform will support AI tools for intelligence, cyber, simulation, and edge computing.

Kratos $KTOS selected Rangeview to develop advanced turbine engine cast components for drone and missile engines.

The Details:

•	Program Goal: Deliver flight-quality superalloy hardware with shorter lead times.

•	Strategic Need: The effort addresses a U.S. casting industrial base gap flagged by the DoD.

•	Production Impact: The agreement supports Kratos’ plans for large-volume engine production.

•	Technical Edge: Rangeview’s process enables complex geometries with cast superalloys at high speed.

Nebius Releases 2025 Sustainability Report as AI Cloud Grows



Nebius $NBIS published its 2025 Sustainability Report, highlighting energy and water efficiency gains as AI cloud capacity expands.

The Details:

•	Energy Efficiency: Average PUE reached 1.25, below the global average of 1.54.

•	Water Use: Liquid-cooled facilities achieved 0.018 L/kWh; designs could avoid 3.3 billion liters per gigawatt.

•	Renewables: Nebius sourced 100% renewable electricity in Iceland, France, and the UK.

•	Community Impact: Nebius Academy partnered with 16 universities on STEM and workforce programs.

T1 Energy $TE announced a $120M private offering of 4.75% convertible senior notes due 2031.

The Details:

•	Use of Proceeds: Funds will support Phase 1 construction and equipment for its G2_Austin solar cell fab.

•	Financing Role: The notes act as a bridge to a larger debt package for remaining Phase 1 capital expenditures.

•	Terms: Interest is payable semi-annually starting Feb. 1, 2027; notes mature Aug. 1, 2031.
